\section{From one weighted row to connected clusters}

Let \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_n\) be positive bad-extension kernels on a common retained
state space and suppose
\begin{equation}
 Q_jV\le qV
\end{equation}
for every exploration history.  If the initial state law \(\nu\) satisfies
\(\nu(V)\le M\), positivity gives
\begin{equation}
 \nu Q_1\cdots Q_n\mathbf 1
 \le \nu Q_1\cdots Q_nV
 \le Mq^n.
\end{equation}
The terminal inequality uses \(V\ge1\).

On a graph of maximum degree \(\Delta\), use the depth-first upper bound
\(\Delta^{2(n-1)}\) for rooted connected sets of size \(n\).  If
\begin{equation}
 e^\alpha\Delta^2q<1,
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\substack{X\ni o\\X\text{ connected}}}
 e^{\alpha|X|}\mathbb P(B_X)
 \le
 \frac{Me^\alpha q}{1-e^\alpha\Delta^2q}.
\end{equation}

At \(\Delta=18\), \(\alpha=0.1\), and the calibrated \(q\),
\begin{align}
 e^{0.1}18^2q&=0.8702225337961371,\\
 \crit=\frac{e^{-0.1}}{18^2}
 &=0.0027927080803578997,\\
 \frac{e^{0.1}q}{1-e^{0.1}18^2q}
 &=0.020695981332153383.
\end{align}
The margin is strict.  Equality at \(q=\crit\) is rejected.

The executable certificate enumerates the exact four-channel bad-chain mass
through length twelve.  Every weighted bound holds; even lengths saturate in
the alternating star model, whereas odd-length bounds retain the entry-cost
slack.
